Fit a failure-rate hazard model with brms

Source: R/discrete-time-hazard-brms.R
fit_hazard.Rd

Assembles the formula and family with build_hazard_spec, the default prior with build_hazard_prior (unless you supply your own), selects the Stan code the custom families need, and hands it all to brms::brm. Anything in ... is forwarded to brm (chains, iterations, cores, backend, initial values, and so on).

Usage

fit_hazard(
  long,
  m_form,
  baseline = "mem",
  dpar_formulas = list(),
  observation = c("interval", "continuous", "mixed"),
  prior = NULL,
  intercept_priors = list(),
  slope_prior = NULL,
  sd_prior = NULL,
  costressors = list(),
  k_sw = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

long

A data frame, the row-per-interval table from build_hazard_data.

m_form, baseline, dpar_formulas, observation

As in build_hazard_spec.

prior

An optional brmsprior for full manual control. When NULL (the default) a weakly-informative prior is built with build_hazard_prior. A supplied prior is used as given, in place of that default rather than merged with it, so any coefficient it leaves out falls back to brms's own default, not the weakly-informative one. To adjust only some priors and keep the rest, use intercept_priors / slope_prior / sd_prior instead of this.

intercept_priors, slope_prior, sd_prior

As in build_hazard_prior, forwarded when the default prior is built (ignored if you supply prior). Each changes only the priors it names and leaves the rest at their defaults, so a user who only calls fit_hazard can retune without building a prior by hand.

costressors

An optional list of costressor objects, as in build_hazard_spec, forwarded to both the formula and the default prior. The same list must have been passed to build_hazard_data, so long carries the z_<name> columns the formula reads. Defaults to none.

k_sw

An optional softening steepness for a threshold function's gate, as in build_hazard_spec. An advanced override: leave NULL (the default) to use the value in M_catalogue. A fit made with a custom value must be reported with the same one.

...

Further arguments forwarded to brms::brm. Any argument it accepts (e.g. chains, iter, cores, backend, init), except formula, data, family, prior and stanvars, which fit_hazard sets itself. See brms::brm for the full set.

Value

A brmsfit, carrying in $rtft the settings it was fitted with: the failure-rate and baseline functions, the observation mode, the reference temperature Tr and reference time tau_ref, the softening steepness, the co-stressors, the ranges of temperature and elapsed exposure time the data cover, and, for each row of long, the individual and the temperature trajectory it belongs to and the elapsed time at which its interval ends. The reporting functions and the checks read them from there, so they are never re-entered by hand.

Details

A missing value in any variable the model uses is an error. brms would drop the rows concerned without saying so, leaving some individuals with only part of their exposure, so remove those individuals or fill in the values first.

Before fitting, the temperature is checked against the reference Tr for the failure rates that take a logarithm or fractional power of Ta - Tr (zeroexp, power, zeropower): these are undefined where the temperature reaches Tr (zeroexp, zeropower) or drops below it (power), so a run that would hit that is stopped with a clear error rather than a cryptic sampler failure.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
path   <- data.frame(path_id = "A", time = c(0, 60), temp = c(20, 35))
checks <- data.frame(path_id = "A", time = seq(0, 60, by = 10))
ind    <- data.frame(id = 1:20, path_id = "A", event = 1,
                     t_upper = sample(seq(10, 60, 10), 20, replace = TRUE))
long   <- build_hazard_data(ind, path, "interval", checks = checks)
fit    <- fit_hazard(long, "exp", chains = 4, iter = 2000, cores = 4)
} # }
